messages:
AcmeDev: hey, started seeing a lot of 502 / 504s hitting the hosted API for our production app, started ~10:12 PST, roughly 40% of requests failing. sample request-id: req_8a3f4b and trace id trace-0a1b2c. endpoint: POST /v1/generate region=us-west-2 using SDK v2.3.2. can we get an immediate look? the errors started after a big batch job (embedding batch of ~12k items)
Ami (support): thanks — sorry you're hitting this. can you paste a curl repro (or SDK call) and the exact timestamps? also your account id? we'll loop in SRE. :eyes:
AcmeDev: account: acme-42. here's a simplified curl that reproduces (we run it from a k8s job inside our VPC):
```\ncurl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"long prompt...","max_tokens":8000}'\n```
Responses are either 502 or hang for ~30s and then 504. attaching the request-id above.
Jordan (sre): pulled edge logs for us-west-2 around 2141590000-2141590100. seeing a spike of upstream 502s from Envoy with messages: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `error reading response body from upstream`. also a number of `stream reset`/`RST_STREAM` for h2 connections.
Jordan (sre): snippets from envoy (sanitized):
```\n[2026-03-15T10:12:12Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 UF, Upstream-reset, x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 35412\n[2026-03-15T10:12:13Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 Upstream-timeout, x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 30013\n```
Rachel (platform): correlation with runtime pods shows a concurrent spike in kv-cache misses and increase in CPU on runtime nodes. also auth-cache (token validation) had a brief reload at 10:11 due to scheduled key rotation. that may have caused auth backend to return 503s and flushed keepalives.
Paul (eng-runtime): looking at model-serving fleet graphs: several model shards in the red (OOMKill count=0 but high GC/compaction) and grpc keepalive drops. the runtime process logs show repeated `broken pipe` when writing streamed responses.
Ami (support): can you paste the exact edge trace headers from the failed response (x-request-id, x-edge-trace)? that will let us join traces.
AcmeDev: got one full failed response headers: `x-request-id: req_8a3f4b`, `x-edge-trace: trace-0a1b2c`, `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 35412`, `x-forwarded-for: 35.202.44.12`. also saw `Server: envoy` and `via: 1.1 redwood-edge`.
Jordan (sre): joint trace shows request made it to runtime, runtime accepted but then connection to runtime worker died ~28s into request. runtime logs show `ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer` around the same time.
Jordan (sre): hypothesis: a cascade caused by large batched requests (12k embeddings) saturating streaming bandwidth and max concurrent h2 streams on certain upstream pods, combined with auth-cache reload that flushed TLS/h2 connections causing a surge of reconnects. reconnect churn exhausts keepalive pools (nginx/edge) and then Envoy begins failing with 502s and returning 504s when wait times hit deadlines.
Paul (eng-runtime): confirming: runtime had a window where `max_concurrent_streams` per connection was being hit on a subset of model shards. our GRPC HTTP/2 connection pool size is configured conservatively to favor latency — when auth reload forced reconnects we ended up with many short-lived connections and some requests lost.
EdgeBot: deploy-bot @channel deploy completed: `runtime-service v1.82.0 -> v1.82.1` at 2141589800 by paul_eng (note: this deploy touched keepalive/transport tweak)
Rachel (platform): interesting — that deploy was ~3 minutes before the spike. that release toggled a transport-level change (shorter keepalive ping interval) to improve idle cleanup. combined with key rotation maybe created a perfect storm.
Ami (support): immediate mitigation suggestions?
Jordan (sre): short-term: 1) rollback the transport tweak we deployed (revert to v1.82.0) or 2) increase edge upstream connection pool and h2 stream limits temporarily, and 3) add a small rate-limit for very large batch requests at edge to protect runtime. I'd start with (2) because rollback touches runtime code paths.
Paul (eng-runtime): we can flip pool limits in the edge config quickly (non-prod change path ~5-10m). I'll also push a hotfix to runtime to better accept in-flight reconnects (graceful drain) but that will take longer.
Ami (support): I'll reply to customer with repro steps we need and ask them to temporarily rate-limit their batch job. also propose a temporary routing fallback: route requests above X tokens to a dedicated pool.
AcmeDev: we can throttle the batch job, doing that now. what should we set X to? we were sending batches of ~12k items (avg prompt ~200 tokens).
Jordan (sre): set batch size to <4k items or shard across time windows for now. we also suggest adding exponential backoff on 502/504.
Paul (eng-runtime): action items: (A) increase edge h2 stream limit and upstream pool size (hot config) — target change applied in 7m; (B) enable a routing rule in us-west-2 to bias heavy streams to less-loaded model shards — putting a canary rule now; (C) runtime hotfix (accepts reconnects gracefully) — ETA 6h.
Rachel (platform): monitoring/alerts: raising transient 502/504 SLO alert to page SRE if >5% for 5m; we need to track customer-visible errors and model-shard load.
Ami (support): messaging to customer: thanks — please throttle to <4k per batch for next 30m, we'll notify when it's safe to resume. we're also applying config changes at edge to reduce 502s.
AcmeDev: throttling now. will report back in 10m if stable. thanks for the quick triage.
Jordan (sre): applied edge pool bump and h2 stream changes at 2141590068 — watching metrics: error rate dropped from 42% -> 6% over the next minute. still seeing occasional 502s correlated with a small subset of runtime pods.
Paul (eng-runtime): kicked runtime canary change to accept reconnects (non-breaking) at 2141590140; canary shows reduced `ConnectionResetError` occurrences.
Rachel (platform): post-mortem notes (first pass): root cause = emergent interaction between (1) transport change in runtime release v1.82.1 that shortened keepalive/transport grace, (2) auth key rotation that flushed h2 connections, and (3) a client-side large batch job that concentrated load. cascade -> keepalive/connect churn -> pool exhaustion -> upstream closed connections -> Envoy 502/504.
Ami (support): customer update: sent. next steps: follow-up PM with runtime to revert or harden transport tweak, add an edge-level protection for very large requests (rate-limit or dedicated path), and coordinate auth rotations to avoid simultaneous infra changes.
AcmeDev: thanks all — after throttling and your edge changes failures dropped to near zero. we'll add backoff and shard our batches. appreciate the help :heart:
